budget_items.what_was_said: Leominster's economic development coordinator said the city runs over 50 events a year with a zero dollars budget for those events, relying on sponsorships and donations.
During COVID, Leominster used ARPA funds for a facade improvement program reimbursing up to 75% of a project cost, with 14 building owners and businesses taking part.
A newsletter sponsor's funds have been redirected into small grants to local businesses, described as $250 grants so far, with hope the fund grows.
The coordinator said she keeps newsletter print runs conservative, printing about 200 copies to avoid waste, distributing the rest online.
The brook and culvert reconstruction project is under construction and grant-funded; FEMA reportedly prioritized it after the 2023 flood.

budget_items.topic: Large development project near Shirley Road
budget_items.what_was_said: A planning board member said an engineering firm plans a large multi-building project near Shirley Road totaling close to 900,000 square feet of floor space, made possible by an earlier water supply protection district bylaw.

decisions.decision: Stephen Wallace to draft a 'minor site plan review' process so simple changes of use in small existing storefronts (no parking increase, no building alterations) would not require full planning board site plan review; would need zoning language amendment for annual town meeting, or a planning board regulation amendment any time via public hearing.
Committee offered to form a sub-quorum working group (two members plus the ex officio member) to assist Stephen Wallace on the site plan review work if helpful.

After consulting town counsel, determined that non-restaurant businesses (e.g., a nail salon, hardware store) may allow customers to BYOB without needing town permission, since Lunenburg has no BYOB regulation for non-restaurant businesses.
Committee noted Lunenburg lacks an advertisement in the North Central Massachusetts visitor guide and should consider adding one to promote town events.

minutes.headline: New Lunenburg planning director floated zoning fixes for small stores; Leominster briefed the committee on outreach.
minutes.summary: Leominster's economic development coordinator, Amanda Curtis, gave the Lunenburg Economic Development Committee an overview of Leominster's marketing, sponsorship, small-business grant, and infrastructure programs. Lunenburg's newly hired planning and economic development director, Stephen Wallace, introduced himself, proposed visitor-guide advertising and a business brochure, agreed to draft a "minor site plan review" process to ease zoning burdens on small storefronts, and, after consulting town counsel, confirmed non-restaurant businesses may allow BYOB without permission. No formal votes were taken except the roll-call adjournment.

what_happened.line: Lunenburg's new planning director agreed to draft a simpler site plan review process for small storefronts.
Town counsel confirmed non-restaurant businesses, such as a nail salon, can let customers bring their own alcohol without town permission.
Leominster's economic development coordinator briefed the committee on that city's marketing, sponsorship, and small-business grant programs.
The committee noted Lunenburg has no listing in the regional visitor guide and should consider one.
No formal votes were taken apart from the roll-call adjournment.

why_it_matters: A simplified site plan review would still need either a zoning language change at annual town meeting or a planning board regulation change through public hearing -- both are points where residents can weigh in.
The BYOB clarification removes a permitting question for small business owners like salons and shops that don't serve food.
Advertising in a regional visitor guide is a discretionary marketing choice the committee is weighing, not yet a budget request.
